title: Spengler leads Nürburgring from pole to flag
dek: Bruno Spengler converted pole into a 6.703-second win for BMW over Edoardo Mortara's Audi at the Nürburgring, moving to within 20 points of Gary Paffett, who finished sixth from 11th on the grid.

chapters.title: Paffett's lead meets BMW's home form
text: The Nürburgring on Sunday 19 August opened the second half of the ten-race 2012 DTM season, seven weeks after the Norisring. There Jamie Green had passed Martin Tomczyk at the last corner to win, and Gary Paffett had fought back from a first-corner spin to fourth, so that he led the standings on 95 points. Green was second on 69, Bruno Spengler third on 58, Tomczyk fourth on 54, and Mattias Ekström, who retired at the Norisring on the first lap, fifth on 47. In between the series had made a non-championship visit to Munich's Olympic Stadium.

Paffett called the first half of his season nearly perfect, with two wins and two further podium finishes, and said he hoped the second half would continue in the same vein. Spengler, the best-placed BMW driver, had won twice in the Eifel before, in sunshine and in pouring rain, but arrived in new territory with the BMW Bank M3 DTM and said he was confident.

The weekend also marked the 40th anniversary of BMW's M brand, which the manufacturer celebrated on the Friday. The race was over 49 laps, 177.821 kilometres, with two rounds of tyre stops, and it was run in heat, with asphalt temperatures around 50 degrees.

chapters.title: Spengler beats the Audis to pole
text: Qualifying was tense to the end. In Q3 Rockenfeller and Filipe Albuquerque were quicker than anyone, with Spengler third, but in the one-lap Q4 shoot-out Spengler produced a 1:24.284 that none of the three Audi drivers alongside him could beat. It was his second pole position of the season, and he said afterwards that his Schnitzer car had not looked good in the morning but the team had turned it around.

Edoardo Mortara of Team Rosberg was the closest, 0.221 seconds slower on 1:24.505 despite running wide at the exit of Turn 2, and his team-mate Albuquerque was third on 1:24.555 with Rockenfeller fourth on 1:24.727. Tomczyk was pushed out of the Q4 places by Albuquerque in the closing seconds and lined up fifth, ahead of Augusto Farfus and Green, who was the best of the Mercedes drivers in seventh.

Dirk Werner, Robert Wickens and Timo Scheider completed the top ten. The big casualty was Paffett, who failed to get out of Q2 and qualified 11th, and Ekström was 12th. Behind them Miguel Molina, Joey Hand, Ralf Schumacher and Adrien Tambay filled the places to 16th, with David Coulthard on the back row in 22nd.

chapters.title: Spengler away, trouble behind
text: Spengler made a good start and was about a second clear by the end of the first lap. Albuquerque made a poor start from third on the grid and fell back, and Tomczyk took advantage to move up to fourth.

Further back there was a chain of incidents on the first lap. Coulthard made contact with Roberto Merhi, who drove into the side of his Persson team-mate Susie Wolff and spun her around. Tambay then spun Molina, and Christian Vietoris spun Priaulx, and both Tambay and Vietoris were handed drive-through penalties that took them out of contention for points. Merhi retired after nine laps, and Tambay, who had completed 14, was the only other driver to stop.

chapters.title: Tomczyk takes third in the stops
text: Mortara held second for most of the race, and eased away from the cars behind him after the first round of stops. Rockenfeller had sat on his tail in the opening stint, but Tomczyk passed the Phoenix Audi shortly after the stops and took the position that became third.

Green was the leading Mercedes driver, and at the second round of stops he took fourth place from Rockenfeller. Paffett, who started 11th, might have been able to join the fight, but a slow second stop left him behind the Audi. He was followed home by Wickens, who stayed close behind him for the closing stint.

chapters.title: Spengler wins by 6.7 seconds
text: Spengler led from the start to the end apart from his own stops, and crossed the line after 49 laps in 1h11m12.847s, 6.703 seconds ahead of Mortara. He also set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:25.185 on lap 31. Tomczyk was third, 10.802 seconds behind, and Green fourth at 22.019 seconds, ahead of Rockenfeller who was fifth.

Paffett took sixth, 23.765 seconds back, and Wickens seventh, his best result of the season. Albuquerque recovered from his poor start to eighth, ahead of Scheider and Farfus, who completed the top ten. Ekström was 11th and Werner 12th. Ralf Schumacher was 13th, Coulthard was the last classified runner, one lap down in 20th.

chapters.title: BMW's first Nürburgring win since 1990
text: Spengler won his second race of the year and the 11th of his DTM career, and BMW's first DTM win in the Eifel in 22 years, since Emanuele Pirro won there in 1990 with a Schnitzer M3. The result fell on the weekend of the M brand's 40th anniversary. "What a dream day," he said, calling the race great fun. BMW's motorsport director Jens Marquardt described a dream weekend: pole on Saturday, then first and third on Sunday. Tomczyk, who had made up places with a strategy and a pass on Rockenfeller, completed the podium.

Mortara, who had been second to Spengler, said he pushed hard but that Spengler was always about a tenth faster. Audi's motorsport chief Wolfgang Ullrich said Mortara had driven a faultless race but had only one fresh set of tyres left after qualifying, unlike the winner, and noted that Audi had four cars in the top ten in the extreme temperatures. It was Mortara's second podium of the season, after his win at the Red Bull Ring. Canadians took first and seventh, with Wickens of Mücke Mercedes finishing seventh.

Mercedes had put three cars in the first seven despite a poor grid. Green said fourth was all he could do, an improvement on qualifying, while Paffett said the car was quick enough for fourth, but a bad pit stop left him behind Rockenfeller. He kept the lead of the championship, though Mercedes' Norbert Haug said the team had done the best with moderate grid positions.

In the standings Paffett led on 103 points, with Spengler up to second on 83, 20 behind, and Green third on 81. Tomczyk was fourth on 69, with Rockenfeller and Mortara level on 49. About 89,000 spectators attended the weekend in the Eifel. With four races left, the series returned to action after only a week, with the next round at Zandvoort in the Netherlands on 26 August.

facts.v: Spengler took pole with 1:24.284, 0.221 seconds clear of Mortara, and set the fastest race lap of 1:25.185 on lap 31.
